cf.title: XMLElement() and XMLForest() embed the XML declaration of xml arguments

input.subject: XMLElement() and XMLForest() embed the XML declaration of xml arguments

verdict_reasoning: No objection to the idea or the design survived for master: the change follows SQL/XML 10.19, xmlconcat(), Oracle and Db2, and it fixes output that xml_in() rejects. The one surviving objection, standards-compat-1, is fixable and concerns the stable target only. A committer who knows the xml code has to decide whether minor releases should change query output.

brief.title: Drop XML declaration of xml values embedded by xmlelement() and xmlforest()
brief.problem: When an xml value with an XML declaration is used as element content, xmlelement() and xmlforest() copy the declaration into the element. A declaration is only allowed at the start of a document, so xml_in() rejects the result and a dump containing it cannot be restored.
brief.proposed_design: The patch adds a flag to xml_out_internal() to omit the declaration. map_sql_value_to_xml_value() uses this flag when it embeds an xml value as element content, which covers xmlelement(), xmlforest() and the query_to_xml() family. Attribute values are not affected.
user_visible_surface: Output of xmlelement() changes: the declaration of an xml argument used as content is no longer copied into the element.
Output of xmlforest() changes in the same way.
Output of the query_to_xml() family changes in the same way.
author_claims: SQL/XML (ISO/IEC 9075-14, sections 6.15, 6.16 and 10.19) puts only the children of the document node into the element, so the declaration is dropped.
Oracle and Db2 also drop the declaration.
xmlconcat() already drops the declarations of its arguments.
The bug only shows when xml_out() would print the declaration, i.e. for a standalone property or a version other than 1.0.
The fix is a bugfix suitable for stable branches, per the CommitFest target version.
brief.thread_state: Only the first message is visible. The author asks for thoughts on the approach.
unclear: The material does not say whether other declaration contents, such as encoding, are also dropped or matter for the result.
The proposal does not say whether a back-patch is safe, given that query results change for existing users.
The material does not say how existing dumps that already contain such values are handled.
The proposal does not say whether other functions that embed xml values, such as xmlagg() or xmlroot(), have the same issue.
The material does not say what the new regression tests cover.

objections.title: Back-patching changes xmlelement() and query_to_xml() output in stable branches
objections.failure_scenario: An application on a minor release stores or compares xmlelement() or query_to_xml() output that contains an embedded declaration, for example to check standalone="yes". After a minor update the same query returns different text without the declaration. The user finds out when a checksum, a diff or a downstream parser that reads the inner declaration gives a different result.
objections.argument: The CommitFest entry targets stable, so the patch changes query results inside a minor release. The current output cannot be read back by xml_in(), which argues for a fix, but the text form is still returned to clients and may be used as text. Message #1 makes the standards case for master but does not say why a minor release should change output. A committer would likely ask whether only master should get the change, with a release note.
objections.author_must_show: Why should stable branches change xmlelement(), xmlforest() and query_to_xml() output, rather than only master with a release note?

critic.reasoning: The CommitFest entry targets stable, and message #1 makes the standards case without weighing a result change in a minor release. The old output fails xml_in(), which favours a fix, but clients still receive it as text, so the question stands.

refuted.title: Back-patching changes xmlelement() output in a minor release
refuted.failure_scenario: A user stores or compares the text output of xmlelement() or query_to_xml() on xml values that have a standalone or non-1.0 declaration. After a minor update the output loses the declaration, and checksums, diffs or downstream lenient parsers see different text without any release-cycle warning.
refuted.argument: The CommitFest entry targets stable branches, but message #1 does not discuss back-patching. The old output was not valid xml, which favours a fix. But Postgres usually avoids changing query results in minor releases unless the old behaviour causes errors or data loss. Here the failure is a dump that does not restore, and the thread does not yet weigh that against the output change.
refuted.author_must_show: Why should this result change go into minor releases instead of master only, given that the broken dumps already exist and the fix does not repair them?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1, which states the same back-patch concern with the same failure scenario and a more concrete request to the author.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch adds a flag to xml_out_internal() in xml.c; the material does not show whether an exported signature changes in stable branches.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: The patch changes xmlelement() and xmlforest() output to follow SQL/XML 6.15, 6.16 and 10.19.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: Stored xmlelement() results with an embedded declaration fail on restore; the patch stops new ones but does not repair existing rows.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The CommitFest entry targets stable, so minor releases would change xmlelement(), xmlforest() and query_to_xml() output.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Why should stable branches change xmlelement(), xmlforest() and query_to_xml() output, rather than only master with a release note?
How should users find and repair rows already stored with an embedded declaration, which still fail on restore after the patch?
Do other functions that embed xml values, such as xmlagg() or xmlroot(), copy the declaration in the same way?
Does it matter for the result that the encoding or a version other than 1.0 in the embedded declaration is dropped?
Does the new flag change the signature of a function that extensions can call in stable branches?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows the xml data type code in xml.c and the back-patch policy would have to own it; none has spoken in the one visible message.
committability.liability: The committer signs for a change of query output in every branch that gets the patch, and for reports from users whose stored or compared text differs after a minor update.
committability.author_follow_up: The author asks for thoughts on the approach in message #1; no other sign either way.

priority.reason: The bug shows only for xml values with a standalone property or a version other than 1.0, but it produces values that do not restore from a dump. The patch is 5.0 KB, touches xml.c and its regression test, and adds no user-visible surface.

provisional_note: Without the code, this review cannot check that attribute values and other callers of xml_out_internal() keep their output, or what the new regression tests cover.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Declarative partitioning
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Simon Riggs, Alvaro Herrera, Robert Haas
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add declarative partitioning to PostgreSQL: a partitioned table kind with a LIST or RANGE partition key, created with CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION BY and CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION OF ... FOR VALUES, with partition key and bound information stored in new catalogs pg_partitioned_rel and pg_partition. Inserts and COPY route tuples to the right partition directly, while many ALTER TABLE operations, triggers, constraints and indexes on partitions are restricted; the WIP patch had no planner support yet.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers asked for planner/optimization support, regression tests, and documentation or README files explaining the design before a full review. Simon Riggs held that the optimization side was the core of the design and recommended "Returned with Feedback" pending that work. Later messages asked for an incremental approach instead of one very large patch, and for a catalog structure and syntax that could later support multi-level partitioning. The CF manager then marked the patch returned with feedback, as the consensus was to rework it further.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The current patch implements a
bunch of stuff, but its hard to say what, how or why it does it and without
the planner stuff its all moot.

precedents_retrieved.title: Declarative partitioning
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds declarative range and list partitioning: a new partitioned relkind created with PARTITION BY, partitions created with CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION OF ... FOR VALUES, and new catalogs pg_partitioned_rel and pg_partition. It also covers multi-level partitioning, attach and detach of partitions, and tuple routing on insert through the parent.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas marked it Returned with Feedback near the 9.6 feature freeze. The last patch was posted on February 17, the entry had been Waiting on Author since March 2, and syntax, scope and performance testing were still open. He said he would review it for 9.7.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Even if we had a
new patch in hand at this point, I don't think there's any real chance
of being able to get this done for 9.6; there are too many things left
to do here in terms of figuring out syntax and scope, and of course
performance testing.

precedents_retrieved.title: ECPG: Declare Statement
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add DECLARE STATEMENT support to ECPG, so that an AT clause given once binds a statement name to a connection. Later PREPARE, EXECUTE, DECLARE CURSOR and similar statements then use that connection without repeating AT, with ecpglib functions such as ECPGdo changed to look up the connection by statement name.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. They end in November 2016 with Michael Meskes waiting for a patch after the design was clarified, and the entry was returned with feedback in November 2017.

precedents_retrieved.title: Added support of XML_PARSE_HUGE flag for XML documents
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch passes the libxml2 XML_PARSE_HUGE flag when Postgres parses XML, which raises the single text node limit from 10,000,000 to 1,000,000,000. It replaces xmlParseBalancedChunkMemory(), which takes no options, with xmlNewNode() plus xmlParseInNodeContext() on a fake root node, and moves from xmlParseMemory() to xmlReadMemory().
precedents_retrieved.objection: The XML_PARSE_HUGE change was committed to HEAD as 2197d06224a1 and then reverted in f2743a7d70e7. The security team found that it lets the backend use large amounts of CPU and memory in cases like the billion laughs attack, even when the application checks input size, because libxml2 does not guarantee input limits under XML_PARSE_HUGE. The author agreed with the revert. The separate replacement of xmlSubstituteEntitiesDefault() with XML_PARSE_NOENT (65c5864d7fac) stayed in.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The security team has discussed 2197d06224a1 after a report from coverity regarding the effects that issues like [1] would create in the backend, and concluded that this patch should be reverted because this could cause the backend to waste plently of CPU and/or memory even if the application applied checks on the size of the data given in input, and libxml2 does not offer guarantees that input limits are respected under XML_PARSE_HUGE.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add XMLCast (SQL/XML X025)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds XMLCAST (SQL/XML X025) to convert between xml and SQL types, mapping SQL types to XML Schema types in their lexical forms (for example interval to xs:duration, timestamp to xs:dateTime). It covers character, numeric, boolean, binary and date/time types and the BY VALUE / BY REF passing mechanism.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch because no reviewer took it up in two years. The author's replies quote Robert Haas asking whether anyone besides the author wanted the feature and saying he did not know the area well enough to commit it. Later review by Marcos Pegoraro covered only documentation and domain handling.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Since there hasn't been any substantial review of this feature in the
past two years, I'll withdraw the patch from the CF to keep things tidy.

precedents_retrieved.title: Propagate sanity checks of ProcessUtility() to standard_ProcessUtility()?
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves the argument sanity checks that ProcessUtility() runs into a macro and also runs them in standard_ProcessUtility(). The goal is to catch extensions that pass bad arguments, such as a NULL query string, down a chain of utility hooks.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas judged that the change saves little debugging time, since a hook that passes bad arguments crashes quickly and a backtrace shows the cause. He also preferred to keep the assertions visible in place of a macro, and noted that such superficial checks would not catch errors in hooks that change the node tree. Michael Paquier did not argue further and the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I can't imagine a scenario where this change saves more than 5 minutes
of debugging, so I'd rather leave things the way they are.

precedents_retrieved.title: plpgsql - possibility to get element or array type for referenced variable type
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets PL/pgSQL `%TYPE` refer to variables of composite type, including polymorphic parameters. It also adds syntax to derive the array type or the element type of a referenced variable, first as `%ARRAYTYPE`/`%ELEMENTTYPE` and later as `%TYPE[]` and `ELEMENT OF ...%TYPE`.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane proposed rejecting this PL/pgSQL-only implementation. He wanted these type operators added to the core grammar's Typename production, so PL/pgSQL would pick them up automatically. Joe Conway and Jim Nasby agreed. The author then found that a reduced patch with only the composite `%TYPE` fix gave too little benefit, and asked for it to be rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I played with the reduced patch, and the benefit without all other things
is negligible. It should be rejected.

precedents_retrieved.title: Relax transactional restrictions on ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE (redux).
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Relax transactional restrictions on ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE (redux).
Reverted commit(s): Revert to 9.6 treatment of ALTER TYPE enumtype ADD VALUE.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Originally committed as 15bc038f (plus some follow-ups), this was
reverted in 28e07270 due to a problem discovered in parallel
workers.  This new version corrects that problem by sending the
list of uncommitted enum values to parallel workers.

Here follows the original commit message describing the change:

To prevent possibly breaking indexes on enum columns, we must keep
uncommitted enum values from getting stored in tables, unless we
can be sure that any such column is new in the current transaction.

Formerly, we enforced this by disallowing ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE
from being executed at all in a transaction block, unless the target
enum type had been created in the current transaction.  This patch
removes that restriction, and instead insists that an uncommitted enum
value can't be referenced unless it belongs to an enum type created
in the same transaction as the value.  Per discussion, this should be
a bit less onerous.  It does require each function that could possibly
return a new enum value to SQL operations to check this restriction,
but there aren't so many of those that this seems unmaintainable.

precedents_retrieved.title: Extending the range operators so they can cope with range <op> element and element <op> range in addition to the existing range <op> range
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch extends the range operators << , >>, &< and &> so that one side may be an element of the range's subtype, in addition to range <op> range. This matches how @> and <@ already accept an element on one side.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding after the patch stopped applying in March 2021 and a rebase was requested. Reviewers found the code clean and Tomas Vondra planned to commit it, but no updated patch came for six months, so the CFM returned it. One early comment questioned whether the new functions were worth the catalog clutter, but that did not decide the outcome.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch needs updates and a rebase and there has been no new patch
six months, so marking Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Replace pg_restrict by standard restrict"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Replace pg_restrict by standard restrict"
Reverted commit(s): Replace pg_restrict by standard restrict
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit f0f2c0c1aef95757c4e7f144d5577e2b0d814279.

The original problem that led to the use of pg_restrict was that MSVC
couldn't handle plain restrict, and defining it to something else
would conflict with its __declspec(restrict) that is used in system
header files.  In C11 mode, this is no longer a problem, as MSVC
handles plain restrict.  This led to the commit to replace pg_restrict
with restrict.  But this did not take C++ into account.  Standard C++
does not have restrict, so we defined it as something else (for
example, MSVC supports __restrict).  But this then again conflicts
with __declspec(restrict) in system header files.  So we have to
revert this attempt.  The comments are updated to clarify that the
reason for this is now C++ only.

precedents_retrieved.title: Embedded server
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Embedded server
Section: Features We Do Not Want
precedents_retrieved.objection: While PostgreSQL clients runs fine in limited-resource environments, the server requires multiple processes and a stable pool of resources to run reliably and efficiently. Stripping down the PostgreSQL server to run in the same process address space as the client application would add too much complexity and failure cases. Besides, there are several very mature embedded SQL databases already available.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P6] is about how xmlconcat() handles processing instructions and DTDs, a different function and question, and it has no recorded reason that could apply to dropping declarations in xmlelement() or xmlforest(). Message #1 points to no earlier discussion of this idea, so the prior-attempts angle has nothing to raise.

The change matches SQL/XML 10.19, xmlconcat() and two other databases, so I have no standards objection to it on master. The only objection concerns back-patching. [P6] is about xmlconcat() and has no recorded reason, so this review does not rely on it.

The patch changes only the text that xmlelement(), xmlforest() and the query_to_xml() family produce, with no change to WAL, catalogs, the wire protocol or extension ABI. Rows already stored with an embedded declaration stay as they are and still fail on restore. The patch does not make that worse, but the release note could tell users how to find and fix such rows.

The patch changes only the serialized output of xmlelement(), xmlforest() and the query_to_xml() family. It adds no privilege, role, setting or exposure path, and it uses no more resources than the current code. Dropping the declaration makes values easier to restore and does not let a user bypass row-level security or column privileges. Without the code, a reader cannot check whether the new flag also affects error messages.

From the maintenance and fit angle the design is small and local to xml.c. It adds no hot-path cost for queries without xml, follows existing xmlconcat() behaviour, and belongs in core. [P6] has no recorded reason and covers a different xmlconcat() change, so it is not cited.

No existing feature gives the same result: xmlelement(), xmlforest() and query_to_xml() produce output that xml_in() rejects, and no extension can fix core output that cannot be restored. [P6] covers PIs and DTDs in xmlconcat(), records no reason, and does not apply to dropping declarations in element content.

This is a correctness bug: xmlelement() can store a value that xml_in() rejects, so a dump with it does not restore. Such a bug needs no demand evidence, and standard text, Oracle, Db2 and xmlconcat() agree on the fix; [P6] has no recorded reason. Whether to back-patch with no field report is left to other angles.
